title: The Aristocats.
lines: In a big house in Paris lives a white cat.
Marie is a white kitten with a pink bow.
Berlioz plays the piano with his little paws.
He makes lovely pictures with paint.
The kittens live with a kind old lady.
Madame loves her cats very much.
Every evening they get a little bowl of warm milk.
A butler lives in the house too.
He doesn't want the cats to get everything.
One evening Edgar does something naughty.
He puts sleeping powder in the milk.
Then Edgar puts them in a basket.
He rides out of the city on his motorbike with the basket.
Far away, by a river, he leaves the basket behind.
When the kittens wake up, they get a fright.
The next morning a cat comes by.
Where do you need to go?
They jump onto the back of a milk lorry.
The kittens secretly lick some of the milk.
They walk across a long bridge.
They stroll over the roofs of the city.
Marie almost falls into the river!
But Thomas jumps in after her.
In the evening they arrive at the house of Thomas's friends.
There's a trumpet, a piano and a double bass.
All the cats dance and sing.
Everybody wants to be a cat, they sing.
Berlioz plays along on the piano.
Toulouse taps along with his tail.
And Marie sings the loudest of all.
The next day they finally arrive in Paris.
He quickly puts them in a big trunk.
He wants to send the trunk far away by train.
Luckily a little mouse has seen everything.
Roquefort runs as fast as he can to Thomas.
The kittens are in a trunk!
The alley cats come to help.
Then Edgar falls into the trunk himself.
The trunk with Edgar inside goes off on the train.
She hugs Duchess and the three kittens.
Would you like to come and live with us?
And Madame does something else kind.
She opens her home to all the cats who don't have a home.
Now lots of cats live with Madame.
There's music every day and warm milk every day.
Marie sings, Berlioz plays the piano and Toulouse paints.
And they live happily ever after.
